title: Pseudomonas & Pf Phage - Tobra vs Cipro
official: 12-week, Open Label, Randomized, Cross-over Study of Inhaled Tobramycin vs Oral Ciprofloxacin in Patients > 12 Years With Cystic Fibrosis, Chronic Pseudomonas Aeruginosa and Pf Bacteriophage Infection
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether Pf bacteriophage (phage) status can be used as a predictive biomarker to guide antibiotic selection and improve treatment response in adolescents and adults with cystic fibrosis and chronic Pf phage-positive Pseudomonas aeruginosa airway infection. Participants must be at least 12 years of age and have chronic P. aeruginosa infection with detectable Pf bacteriophage in sputum.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does treatment with oral ciprofloxacin result in greater improvement in lung function (FEV1) than inhaled tobramycin in participants with Pf phage-positive P. aeruginosa infection?
* Can Pf phage status predict clinical and microbiologic response to antibiotic therapy, including changes in bacterial density, airway inflammation, and respiratory symptoms?

Researchers will compare inhaled tobramycin and oral ciprofloxacin in a randomized crossover design to determine whether participants with Pf phage-positive infection respond better to an antibiotic that is not predicted to be sequestered by Pf phage.

Participants will:

* Complete a 12-week randomized crossover study receiving both inhaled tobramycin and oral ciprofloxacin during separate treatment periods.
* Provide sputum samples for bacterial culture, bacterial density measurements, and inflammatory biomarker analyses.
* Provide blood samples for inflammatory biomarker analyses and safety monitoring
* Undergo pulmonary function testing, including spirometry for measurement of FEV1 and lung clearance index measurements.
* Complete quality-of-life assessments and undergo routine clinical and safety monitoring, including blood testing and anthropometric measurements.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥ 12 years.
* Diagnosis of cystic fibrosis
* Chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, defined as \>50% of respiratory cultures positive during the previous 12 months
* Detection of Pf bacteriophage in sputum.
* Ability to perform spirometry reliably.
* Willingness and ability to comply with study procedures and visits.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Previous lung transplantation.
* Current systemic antibiotic treatment for a pulmonary exacerbation.
* History of intolerance to sputum collection or sputum induction procedures.
* Current treatment for non-tuberculous mycobacterial infection.
* Current treatment for Burkholderia infection
* Unwillingness to discontinue current inhaled antibiotic therapy for the required 4-week washout period.
* History of prolonged QT interval or cardiac disease.
* Currently taking QT prolonging medication, or specifically if taking azithromycin has baseline QTc \> 450 msec.
* Currently taking theophyllline, duloxetine, or zolpidem.
* Significant lab abnormalities.
* Current pregnancy.
* Currently breastfeeding.
